description:
Team Muyuy 🌱🛰️

We are a team working on “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data”. Muyuy is a Quechua word meaning “to turn”. It is also the name of the traditional Andean system of crop rotation.

We’re building a decision-support tool that uses NASA Earth data to help farmers compare crop rotation strategies and see the benefits, trade-offs and risks of each one. It works offline and edge-to-edge, so the data reaches farmers in areas without internet.
summary:
🌱 Muyuy (Quechua for “to turn”) is an offline-first mobile app that helps smallholder farmers choose more resilient crop rotations using NASA Earth data.

🛰️ Muyuy is designed to turn 40 years of NASA POWER records into a local agro-climatic calendar (frost risk, rainfall, evapotranspiration and water balance) adjusted for altitude, which is critical in the Andes. A deterministic, transparent rotation engine combines this calendar with crop requirements based on FAO ECOCROP and agronomic rules, and compares the farmer’s current practice with alternatives. It scores each option on water use, soil health, income and climate risk, and shows its confidence per factor and whether the zone is locally validated. AI only writes the plain-language explanation; it never chooses or scores.

📲 The app is built to work without internet, using small data packages designed to travel phone-to-phone.

📍 Pilot region: Huánuco, Peru.
details:
🌱 Muyuy — NASA data for the last field

The problem

In the Peruvian Andes, frost, erratic rain and tired soils put every harvest at risk. NASA has decades of climate data that could help, but it rarely reaches the farm: it is technical, scattered, and many farmers have no internet signal.

What Muyuy does

Muyuy (Quechua for “to turn”, the traditional Andean rotation system) is an offline-first app that helps smallholder farmers choose more resilient crop rotations. The farmer picks their field, current crops and priorities, and Muyuy shows:

  • A monthly agro-climatic calendar: frost risk, rainfall, evapotranspiration and water balance.
  • Their current rotation vs. better alternatives, scored on water, soil health, income and climate risk.
  • A plain-language explanation, confidence per factor, and what a local expert should verify.

The app recommends; the farmer decides.

How it works

  1. Prepare (cloud): 40 years of NASA POWER data become a local calendar, corrected for altitude. The raw grid placed Huánuco city ~1,500 m too high, which would have made a warm valley look like cold highlands. A deterministic engine combines it with crop requirements based on FAO ECOCROP and rotation rules. AI only writes the explanations.
  2. Distribute: results are packed into a ~5 KB verified data package that travels phone-to-phone where there is no signal.
  3. Use (100% offline): the app ranks rotations by the farmer’s own priorities, even in airplane mode.
  4. Return: with signal, field reports are validated against NASA data and neighbors’ reports to improve the next package.

Science and validation

  • Rules verified by automated tests: every rotation rule (frost, rain, family repetition) is covered by unit tests.
  • Altitude correction validated: NASA's grid placed Huánuco ~1,500 m too high; we correct it with real elevation (Open-Meteo).
  • O deja la línea como meta: Next step: measure accuracy against MIDAGRI crop statistics (target 80–90%).

Benefits and impact

Muyuy turns satellite data into decisions farmers can act on, for free, without an account or internet. It encourages rotations that break pest cycles, restore nitrogen and protect soil. Piloted in Huánuco’s highlands, valleys and rainforest, the same approach works anywhere with just coordinates.

Creativity and tools

Ancestral rotation wisdom meets NASA satellites, and data “walks” from phone to phone like news in a rural community. Built with Flutter, Java/Quarkus, Python, PostgreSQL, Three.js and Groq (gpt-oss-120b), on Oracle Cloud and GitHub Actions.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources)
